item.title: The Daily Blogroll — Friday, 27 November 2026
item.description:
Anarchae tweaks a self-imposed Shin Megami Tensei V: Vengeance challenge after brutal fights, then dives into Shinagawa quests, demons, and lore speculation.

Sey rounds up Apple Crumble, Am I Nima, Waltz and Jam, and TANUKI’s stacked soundtrack while juggling a giant RPG and year-end indie overload.

Kimimi finds Soma Bringer broadly fine but frustratingly bland, with forgettable story beats and mushy combat that never gives its ideas enough bite.

Ramen Junkie says Presto is the standout Dungeons and Dragons figure, mostly thanks to clever hat-based magic accessories that outshine the line’s usual limits.

Joar is happily living in WoW delves and Coiled Isle side quests, while his usual alt-leveling obsession takes a surprising break.

Ellie revisits Metal Gear Solid 2 with clear affection, spotlighting Kojima’s flashier, sillier stealth sequel and its earnest war-and-nukes obsession.

Wilhelm weighs how EverQuest Legends and WoW Forever might turn nostalgia servers from a big event into a permanent, less magical MMO market fixture.

Tobold argues America’s two-party system turns frustrated anti-incumbent voting into a coin flip, making 2028 far less settled than midterms suggest.

Bruce Schneier says the Microsoft, FAA, bank, United, NSA, and Apple outages look less like conspiracy than capitalism starving infrastructure resilience.

Cristian points out a real Fediverse headache: ActivityPub is great, but finding Pixelfed or WriteFreely accounts from Mastodon is still awkward.

The Friendly Necromancer shares how MRI noise, music therapy, and a stage 4 lung cancer diagnosis shaped songs on Cosmic Radiation and Bad Luck.

Blockade85 checks in from holiday chaos, squeezed schedules, and a fresh FFXIV caster run, with A Realm Reborn still feeling stubbornly slow.

item.title: The Daily Blogroll — Thursday, 26 November 2026
item.description:
Kelly argues Ace Combat 8 ranking the F35 over the Gripen says little about what actually makes sense for Canada’s real fighter choice.

Patrick drops 37,000 words of Veins of the Earth settlement tables for VotE ReMastered, plus a sale and a call for feedback.

Joel dives back into Breath of the Wild and nails why wandering Hyrule, improvising around danger, and chasing vistas still feels so good.

Krista finds Duck Side of the Moon a charmingly cosy space adventure, with ship upgrades, crop-growing, wholesome quests, and yes, a quack button.

Emily fondly revisits finally beating Lilo & Stitch’s Junkyard Beast on GBA—a backseat-of-the-car victory that clearly stuck for years.

Wilhelm is finally settling on WoW Forever specs across six alts, while a newly added warlock already feels rough enough to bench.

The Chronicler teaches Taifa through an El Cid playthrough, pitching it as a breezy, backstabby medieval Spain card-driven wargame with serviceable bots.

Sweetie shares a candid life update about burnout, health struggles, driving lessons, and how a Miku Expo trip helped recharge her writing brain.

Jeff tracks Ansible’s Ubuntu 26 sudo timeout to sudo-rs prompt changes, and the fix is basically update Ansible or switch become_exe.

Dave Winer sketches a blog-and-RSS-powered Markdown web, with RSS.chat, BonBon customization, and a push for smaller, self-sufficient publishing tools.

Bhagpuss kicks off a loose rereading project with The Crying of Lot 49, sparked by old bookshelves, a dog fetch routine, and pure whim.

Tofutush unpacks how the song 苍蝇 maps onto Bai’e’s worldview, power, surveillance, and self-mythologizing as something bigger than human.

item.title: The Daily Blogroll — Wednesday, 25 November 2026
item.description:
Anarchae digs deeper into SMT V: Vengeance, from Oni and crow demons to Yoko, Tao, and the route’s darker Chaos-leaning themes.

UltrViolet says GTA VI is enormous, polished, and maybe the decade’s best, while still being unmistakably Grand Theft Auto.

Bhagpuss is hooked by Wuthering Waves’ Second Coming of Solaris, though the save system and unpredictable long scenes make sessions run long.

Mailvaltar finds ArcheAge’s Gunslinger too short-ranged and awkward solo, so it’s back to Ebonsong for now and more interest in trading.

Wilhelm’s WoW Forever group came back stronger, cleared Hall of Thanes smarter, and finally put Magmatus down after learning the rough spots.

Ramen Junkie likes this Transformers One Optimus Prime for its surprisingly clever transformation and solid truck mode, even if the scale feels off.

Joar uses AI less like an agent and more like a personal scanner for news, teaching leads, household deadlines, and travel ideas.

Juhis shares practical Advent of Code debugging advice, stressing example inputs, smaller tests, and tighter feedback loops over flailing at full data.

Bruce Schneier points to Daniel Meissler’s effort to track AI-assisted hacking incidents and the offensive tools attackers are using.

Dave Winer keeps pushing BonBon forward with stylesheet and page-handler docs, new Windows and Raspberry builds, and a pitch to Markdown editor developers.

Cristian shares a brief video post on disappearing in 2027, with the whole thing essentially being the embedded clip.

item.title: The Daily Blogroll — Tuesday, 24 November 2026
item.description:
Anarchae’s SMT V: Vengeance notes cover Kamiyacho bosses, demon sidequests, and self-imposed Nahobino restrictions that barely dent an endgame roster.

Roger digs into LOTRO Questa’s NPC identification problem, weighing zone clues, dialogue parsing, and voice analysis to fill database gaps.

Frostilyte expected a quick Denshattack run, then lost nearly 50 hours chasing manuals, combos, and those higher medal thresholds.

Shintar says WoW Forever feels less min-maxed than Classic, with starter-zone hunter pets hinting at lots of new or casual players.

Scopique reshuffles a Star Citizen fleet after IAE 2956, landing on the Gatac Hyun as a standout solo mining-and-salvage ship.

Wilhelm wants Over the Hill to add multiple save profiles and vehicle-by-vehicle trail tracking, which sounds like catnip for completionists.

Tobold contrasts GTA 6 as a finished purchase with Crusader Kings III as an ongoing DLC project that gets pricey fast for lapsed players.

Joel’s weeknotes mix Gunpla, guitar repairs, and a new Switch 2, but Breath of the Wild clearly devoured the week.

Bruce Schneier argues this week’s outages show brittle digital infrastructure is really an incentives problem, with resilience cut in pursuit of profit.

Dave Winer says BonBon’s next step is writing, betting open formats can spare writing tools from wrestling with fractured platform limits.

Cristian shares a YouTube video about 31 practical Claude use cases for 2027, more pointer than deep dive.

item.title: The Daily Blogroll — Monday, 23 November 2026
item.description:
Anarchae starts a fourth Shin Megami Tensei V: Vengeance run and happily dives into Tokyo Tower progress, side quests, and lore-heavy story speculation.

Sey counters Grand Theft Auto VI fever with five crime-flavored indies, from Retro City Rampage and Shakedown: Hawaii to Promise Mascot Agency.

Bhagpuss side-eyes the Grand Theft Auto VI takeover of blogland, while admitting Lana Del Rey hosting an in-game radio station is weirdly tempting.

Marc revisits MadWorld to ask why ultra-violent Wii games felt like smart bets, even when niche realities kept that market smaller than hoped.

Wilhelm rounds up Fantasy Critic chaos as Grand Theft Auto VI drops a monster 98.7 and steamrolls a week otherwise crowded with small PC indies.

The Chronicler digs into Coast Watchers after three plays, highlighting its hidden-information spy-vs-patrol design and strong South Pacific intelligence theme.

Tobold finds low-level Pathfinder: Kingmaker spellcasters weirdly incentivized to use crossbows, especially once digital combat pacing burns through spell slots.

Warner’s weekly reading stack is a pretty grim but sharp tour through AI anxiety, tech failures, and politics getting uglier together.

Juhis has a low-output Djangonaut week, but still finds perspective, team camaraderie, and a nice community win around Django and Raffaella Suardini.

Bruce Schneier argues AI companies keep dodging accountability by treating chatbot output as protected speech when convenient and mere machine error otherwise.

Dave Winer shares fresh BonBon progress, WordPress integration plans, and a bigger pitch for a simpler Markdown-based web for writers.

Kimimi gets candid about Twine nerves, reminding herself that interactive fiction is still real design even when it looks like just words and choices.
